concepts.title: What Social Science Studies
concepts.definition: Social Science explores people, places and events: it studies how humans live together, how societies and states organise, how economies work and how the past shapes the present - building on the stories explored in Grades 6 to 8.
concepts.key_idea: People, places and events studied together: social science reads society like a text.
question_patterns: name the branches of social science and their concerns
how do stories of people and places help us understand society
why is the study of society important for citizens
how does the past shape the present according to social science
distinguish history, geography and economics as social sciences

solution_steps.explain: Social science takes human society as its object of study.
History, geography, political science and economics each view society differently.
Together they explain how people live, govern and earn.

concepts.title: Methods of Studying Society
concepts.definition: Social scientists work with evidence - sources, maps, data and field studies - asking questions of the past and present, comparing viewpoints and reasoning from evidence rather than opinion.
concepts.key_idea: Evidence first, opinion later: social science argues with sources and data.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest101.txt sections on methods of study
question_patterns: what kinds of evidence do social scientists use
how do maps help in studying society
why must conclusions in social science rest on evidence
describe how a historian works with sources
compare the methods of an economist and a geographer
frame a social science question from your surroundings

solution_steps.explain: Sources, statistics and field observation supply the material.
Interrogate the evidence from multiple viewpoints.
Arguments stay tied to the evidence collected.

concepts.title: Why Social Science Matters for Citizens
concepts.definition: Studying society equips citizens to understand rights and duties, judge public policies, respect diversity and participate in democracy; the discipline trains informed, questioning and responsible members of the community.
concepts.key_idea: Informed citizens are made, not born: social science builds the toolkit.
question_patterns: how does social science make us better citizens
why should students learn about democracy and economy
how does social science help in understanding diversity
what skills does the study of society build
connect a social science idea to a current public issue
how can you use social science in daily decision-making

solution_steps.explain: Knowledge of society, polity and economy informs opinions.
Questioning, comparing and reasoning are civic skills.
Informed participation completes the citizen's role.

questions: Name the branches of social science with one question each asks.
How do social scientists use evidence?
Explain the importance of social science for citizens.
